newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Transpower reports yr net surplus NZ$95.9 mln.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Transpower reports yr net surplus NZ$95.9 mln.

text.p: New Zealand's state-owned national electricity grid operator Transpower on Thursday reported an annual net surplus attributable to shareholders of $95.9 million, up from $84.5 million in 1995.

However, Transpower made an economic loss of NZ$47.3 million versus a loss of $2.28 million in 1995. This reflected high underlying interest rates which saw the after-tax cost of operating capital rise by $37 million to $246 million.
In addition, the holding gain from the revaluation of fixed assets contributed $20 million less to the total return on operating capital than in the preceding period.
Transpower said it was moving to introduce economic value statements into the annual report in addition to the traditional reporting of accounts.
Its economic reporting approach was a measure of the extent to which Transpower had achieved the level of return that an investor would expect to compensate for the risk of their investment.
It said when a business performed below the shareholders' fair and reasonable rate of return expectations, it had suffered a "loss of shareholder value", and vice versa.

"Economic reporting is based on the concept that most shareholders want management to create value for them by continually striving to earn a rate of return higher than that considered to be efficient," Transpower said.
"The cumulative loss/gain of economic value provides a useful self-regulatory mechanism for Transpower."
The company said the cost of maintaining and operating its assets had fallen to NZ$116 million from $119 million in the year to June 30.
"This helped us reduce the overall cost of transmitting electricity on the national grid from 1.58 cents/kWh (kilowatt hour) to 1.56 cents/kWh in real terms," it said.

Transpower said tight controls over the past year saw total operating expenses fall at a time when additional resources had to be put in place for development of systems to support the wholesale electricity market.
